key_finding: `syn::TypeTuple.elems` for a 1-element tuple `(u64,)` holds exactly one element (`u64`) -- the trailing comma that syntactically distinguishes a real 1-tuple from a merely-parenthesized type is not itself an element of `elems`. `type_spelling`'s `Type::Tuple` arm joined `elems` with `", "` and wrapped in parens unconditionally, so a 1-element tuple rendered as `"(u64)"` -- byte-identical to what the sibling `Type::Paren` arm renders for a genuinely different type, a merely-parenthesized `u64` (exactly the same type as plain `u64`). Since `type_spelling`'s output feeds `TypeIdentity.name` directly, and `TypeIdentity.canonical` stays `None` throughout this extractor's current scope (this module's own doc comment) so `identity_key()` hashes on `name` alone, two real, structurally different Rust types -- a tuple type accessed via `.0` versus plain `u64` -- collapsed onto the exact same `TypeIdentity` record_id and therefore the same graph Type node whenever they appeared in the same scope. This is a real identity-correctness defect, not a cosmetic rendering nit: it could make the graph treat a real type change (refactoring a field/parameter/return type from `(u64,)` to `(u64)`, or vice versa) as a no-op, or merge two structurally distinct fields' Type nodes into one.
verification_before_acting: Read type_spelling's real, current Type::Tuple and Type::Paren arms directly in adapter/src/semantic/rust/spelling.rs, confirming the exact rendering collision the subagent described.

Read TypeIdentity's real struct definition and identity_key() implementation in core/src/semantic/types.rs directly, confirming identity_key() hashes on `name` (plus repository/revision/scope/canonical) with no other disambiguating field, and that `canonical` is genuinely always None per spelling.rs's own module doc comment -- so this is a real, reachable identity collision, not merely a theoretical one blocked by some other field.

Confirmed via reading adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs's real call sites (field/parameter/return-type TypeIdentity construction) that type_spelling's output is exactly what feeds TypeIdentity.name, with no intermediate disambiguation.

Checked the existing type_spelling_renders_common_shapes_cleanly test and confirmed it only covers a two-element tuple ((u64, u64)) and never exercises a one-element tuple or Type::Paren at all -- a genuine, previously-uncovered gap.

design_decisions.question: How to restore the distinguishing trailing comma?
design_decisions.decision: Special-case tuple.elems.len() == 1 to append a trailing comma (`"({elems},)"`), matching exactly how `rustfmt`/real Rust source always prints a 1-tuple. This is the minimal, correct fix -- multi-element tuples already produce unambiguous output (`"(u64, u64)"` cannot collide with any Paren-arm output, since Paren only ever wraps exactly one inner type) and the empty-tuple case (`()`) is already handled separately and correctly.
